analysis:
The PR replaces the single-threaded uncached read-then-hash loop in WeightHasher.hashSingleFileUncached (WeightHasher.swift:250-259) with OverlappedFileDigest (new file). A dedicated reader thread preads into two alternating 4 MiB page-aligned buffers, and the caller hashes them in order. This changes performance only. The SHA-256 is still computed over the same bytes in file order, so the weight-hash integrity inputs (T-012, T-027, A-004) are unchanged. The per-file digest aggregation, sorting and fallback chain are untouched.

I traced the handoff protocol. Both `free` semaphores are signaled at the start and `filled` starts at 0. The reader waits on free[slot], runs pread (retrying on EINTR), stores the length, then signals filled[slot]. It exits on a count of 0 or less. The caller waits on filled[slot] and returns the digest on 0 or nil on a negative count (read error). A short read greater than 0 is handled by advancing the offset by the bytes actually read. The `defer { readerExited.wait() }` at line 59 guarantees the reader has stopped before the caller closes the descriptor, so there is no use-after-close. The finalized digest is computed before the defer runs. No semaphore is deallocated below its initial value. Buffers and `lengths` are freed only in deinit, after both threads are finished with them. The semaphore operations provide the needed memory ordering for the @unchecked Sendable class.

Failure behavior stays fail-closed. A directory yields EISDIR and a FIFO yields ESPIPE, both returning nil, and the caller then falls back as before. A mid-file read error returns nil rather than a partial hash. The unreadable-file and missing-file tests still apply. A file mutated during hashing behaves as it did before.

Availability: one extra thread per concurrently hashed file, and 8 MiB of buffers per file. With at most 4 workers this is bounded and modest (T-016 and T-029 are not materially affected). The docs update in docs/reference/model-registry-format.md is descriptive only. The new tests cover chunk boundaries, buffer wraparound and concurrent readers. No new trust boundary or attack surface was found. Nothing remains for integration to follow up.
